collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder wants to teach a grandchild to carve, but the child loves stars instead: insist, or follow the child's interest.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has waited years to teach (subject.his/her) grandchild (friend) to carve, as (subject.his/her) own grandparent taught (subject.him/her). But (friend) only wants to lie on the beach at night and count the stars. Every carving lesson ends with (friend) staring at the sky. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) keeps at it. (friend) learns, unwillingly, and carves a very rough star. (subject) sighs, then laughs, and says that is a start. The next lesson, (subject) asks (friend) to tell (subject.him/her) the names of the stars while they carve.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) puts down the knife and lies on the beach beside (friend). (friend) points out the stars (friend.he/she) has named. (subject) points out the ones (subject.his/her) grandparents named. They do this every clear night. Years later, (friend) carves a star chart.
